Translation goal: reverse-translatability for the Tafsir reader — readers should be able to map English back to JA. Saadia-specific moves preserved per data-source/saadia-gloss-table.json; Blau's notes (data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json) consulted for Bereshit 1-12.

translations.1: Let the inhabitants of the heavens be silent, that I may speak; and let the inhabitants of the earth hear the words of my mouth.
translations.2: My discourse shall pour forth like rain, and my utterance shall fall like dew — like a shower upon open spaces, and like drizzle upon the grasses.
translations.3: For I call you by the name of God — so give greatness to our Lord.
translations.4: The Creator — upright is His work; all His conduct is by judgment; the Capable One, possessed of faithfulness, no wrong is with Him; He is the just, the upright.
translations.5: They corrupted before Him — not like His faithful ones; rather they are the fault-finders: a generation that is stubborn and twisted.
translations.6: Is it to God that you repay with these deeds, O people ignorant and unwise? Is He not your Originator, who possesses you? He made you and perfected you.
translations.7: Nay, remember the days of eternity, and understand the years of generation upon generation; ask your father and he will inform you, your elders and they will tell you.
translations.8: That the Most High, when He allotted the nations and dispersed the sons of Adam, set the boundaries of the nations according to the count of the sons of Israel.
translations.9: For the chosen portion of God is His people, and the house of Jacob is His preferred one and His special possession.
translations.10: He sustained him in the land of the wilderness, and in the wandering waste of the open expanse; He encompassed him and enlightened him, and kept him as the pupil of His eye.
translations.11: And like the eagle when it stirs its nest and hovers over its fledglings — it spreads its wings and takes them up and bears them upon its plumage.
translations.12: So God alone guided him, and there were no other objects of worship with Him.
translations.13: And He mounted him upon the heights of the earth, until he ate of the produce of the meadows; and as if He had suckled him with milk from the rock, and honey from the hard flint.
translations.14: And the butter of cattle, and the milk of the flock, together with the fat of lambs, and rams of the breed of Bashan, and he-goats — together with the finest of ground wheat; and the blood of the grape he would drink as an intoxicating drink.
translations.15: And when the one thus described grew fat, he gave himself over to excess — for it was said to him: 'You have grown fat, and become thick, and become coarse' — and he forsook the God who made him, and put to the test the One he relied upon for his deliverance.
translations.16: And they set about provoking Him with foreigners, and with abominations they angered Him.
translations.17: They sacrifice to demons — which are no divinities — objects of worship that they did not know; things new, that came from nearby, and which the worthy men of your fathers did not regard.
translations.18: And so it was said to him: 'The Creator, your Originator, you forget, and the Capable One, your Begetter.'
translations.19: And when God saw that, He rejected them — on account of what had angered Him from them: the sons and the daughters.
translations.20: And He said: 'I shall conceal My mercy from them; I shall show them what their end shall be — for they are a generation of reversals, sons in whom there is no faithfulness.'
translations.21: And just as they provoked Me with what is no god, and angered Me with their vanities — so I shall provoke them with what is no people, and with a clan devoid of knowledge I shall anger them.
translations.22: For fire is kindled from My anger, and it burns down to the lowest depth of the earth; and it consumes the earth and its vegetation, until it reaches the foundations of the mountains.
translations.23: So shall I increase upon them evils, and My arrows I shall scatter among them:
translations.24: the fever of hunger, and burning heat, and bitter sudden death; and the teeth of beasts I shall loose upon them, together with the venom of the crawling things of the dust.
translations.25: And outside, the bereaving sword; and dread from within the chambers — striking down youth and maiden alike, the suckling together with all those of hoary age.
translations.26: And I had said: 'I shall reduce their number as they deserve, and cause their memory to cease from among the people.'
translations.27: But for My taking precaution against the scheming of the enemy — lest their enemies deny this, lest they say: 'Our hand has prevailed, and it was not God who did all these things to them' —
translations.28: for they are a clan that has squandered wisdom, and there is no understanding in them.
translations.29: And would that they were wise, they would have comprehended both, and by those two things would understand their fate.
translations.30: And that is for them to say: 'How could one pursue a thousand, and two put a myriad to flight, were it not that their mainstay had delivered them over, and God had made it possible to overpower them?'
translations.31: For their mainstay is not like our mainstay — nor do our enemies comprehend this.
translations.32: For they are punished as though their vine were from the vine of Sodom, and from the tendrils of Gomorrah; so their grapes are grapes of poison, and their clusters are bitter to them.
translations.33: And like the venom of serpents is their wine, and the poison of the spotted viper — the ferocious among them.
translations.34: Yet all that is treasured away with Me, and sealed in My storehouses.
translations.35: Mine is the vengeance and the full recompense, at the time when their foot shall slip — for how near is the day of their misery, and how swiftly come are the things prepared for them.
translations.36: When God shall render judgment for His people, and grant pardon to His servants — when He shall see that the power has gone from them, and those left, whether confined or abandoned, are all broken under their oppression.
translations.37: When the enemy shall say: 'Where is their God, the Mainstay upon whom they relied?'
translations.38: 'Those who would eat the fat of their sacrifices and drink the wine of their libations — let them arise now and help you; let them be a shield over you.'
translations.39: Look now — I am He alone, and there is no other god with Me; I put to death and I give life; however long I have weakened, I have ever been healing; and there is none who can deliver from My hand.
translations.40: And I swear by the heavens and I say: by My everlasting continuance —
translations.41: I shall whet the gleam of My sword, and My hand shall hold judgment; and I shall bring vengeance upon My enemies, and the dread upon those who hate Me.
translations.42: As if I were making My arrows drunk from their blood, and My sword were consuming their flesh — that it may be sated from the blood of the slain and the captive, from the heads of the rulers of the enemy nations.
translations.43: Praise, O you nations, His people — for He shall avenge the blood of His servants, and shall return that vengeance upon His enemies, and shall grant forgiveness to His land and His people.
translations.44: And it was Moses, when he addressed the people with this hymn of praise — he and Hoshea son of Nun.
translations.45: And when Moses had finished addressing them with this speech,
translations.46: he said to them: 'Turn your minds to all the words by which I solemnly charge you today, that you command your children to observe and to perform all the matters of this Torah —
translations.47: for it is no empty speech for you; rather it is your very life, and by it your span of days shall be lengthened in the land which you are crossing the Jordan to possess.'
translations.48: Then God spoke to Moses on that very same day, saying:
translations.49: 'Go up to this mountain of the Hebrews — Mount Nebo — which is in the land of Moab, which faces Jericho; and behold the land which I am giving to the sons of Israel as a possession.
translations.50: And die on the mountain to which you are ascending, and be gathered to your people — just as Aaron your brother died on Mount Hor, and was gathered to his people —
translations.51: on account of what you two caused: the nation's breach of faith in Me, in the midst of the sons of Israel, at the contention of Raqim in the wilderness of Zin — in that you did not sanctify Me in their midst.
translations.52: Therefore you shall behold the land from the opposite side — but you shall not enter it, the land which I am giving to the sons of Israel.'
